Difficult one to review for me. I really wanted to like this one!

The game seems alright mechanically, but a few major things hold it back.

After over ten hours, I'm still stuck with only two characters. The game promises complex theorycrafting, but it seems like it will take ages to get there. Currently I can't say, even with a dozen hours played, that a single build has come online.

The early game is marred by overpowered allies. In almost all story missions, some random hero will join your team and clear the map for you. Even on hard difficulties. It's a very odd design choice that I don't stand by. I'd rather build my own team from scratch.

Unlocking masteries and sets thereof isn't transparent. So you'll have to consult a guide if you want to make a specific build happen. Not a huge issue, but it's an odd choice and seems like it will add an element of grind to the game.

The base building aspect isn't exciting at all.

The UI is quite clunky, especially on Steam Deck.

Many missions seemed quite repetitive to me, and too often you have hordes of enemies coming at you. It feels more grindy than tactical.

Worst of all is the writing. The game has a lot of dialogue screens with filler discussion. Think "..." "..." over and over again. The story has made very little sense so far. I would be tempted to skip it altogether. The translation is even worse. It seems like it is a literal (machine?) translation from Korean and much of it simply makes no sense in English. Why not hire a competent translator?

Beyond all this, I'm sure there is a great game to be discovered here if you can dedicate tens of hours to get the game even started. I don't think I can find it in me to do that, especially considering the other reservations above.

The game was recommended to me as a XCOM-like with deeper buildcrafting. That it ultimately might be, but I can't say I found the first ten hours exciting enough to continue.

If it's on sale, I would recommend trying it, regardless.

After 200 hours I think it's fair to say I've got plenty TO say about this game. The long and short of it is that while this title probably isn't for everyone, if it's something you enjoy you're going to have a great time.  For me this was a solid 9/10.  

This game is a tactical turn based RPG in the isometric style of FF tactics, Fire Emblem, etc.  Characters will move in turn across a grid battlefield and perform actions selected by the player, most often with the goal of defeating the enemy units on the field.  When the player is not in combat they will manage a roster of characters by equipping gear and changing their abilities to develop a strategy that will allow that character to maximize their impact in battle.  Effective gameplay involves making the right decisions, both in and out of combat, and mistakes are punished accordingly.  There is no time limit on making decisions, so it's important to plan ahead and act with a strategy in mind.  Combat missions often have you extremely outnumbered, so many of them can take a significant amount of time to complete. 

This title stands out from its competition by doing a few things differently: 
1: There are a ton of simple mechanics to learn that will all be necessary to master the game.  The game's systems seem expansive, but they are surprisingly easy to learn.  In my opinion this was a great design choice, as it helps to keep the learning curve smooth and manageable.  The end result is a level of character customization that is unmatched by just about any other title in this genre on the market.  
Systems include: Gear crafting, gear sets with set bonuses, monster taming (catch a wild creature to assist you in combat), machine building (get your own custom robot pet), targeted farming via story replay and extra missions if you need money or certain types of items, Character classes (with the ability to save multiple loadouts per character if you like to switch things up), multiple layers of passive abilities (most of which apply to the individual character, but some that also apply to the entire team), passive ability set bonuses (if you have certain combinations equipped you get bonus effects) and more!

2: Many missions allow you to utilize generic police units to assist you in combat. These units can be controlled directly, or set to a few different automatic behaviors if you don't want to bother.  Unlike a lot of other games, these units are actually quite helpful in tougher missions.  While they are unlikely to win the fight on their own, they provide enough assistance to make them feel like highly trained police officers, and valuable assets on the field. 

3: Random enemies.  Many missions (especially side missions) have rare enemies that pop up occasionally.  These enemies offer unique rewards (like special passive abilities or crafting materials) that can help keep farming interesting.  

4: Optional engagement.  While the game has a ton of systems, on its easiest difficulty there's really no need to take full advantage of them.  However, the more you learn the game the more you'll want to farm to engage with it.  This game doesn't hold your hand when it comes to learning how to optimize your characters, so figuring out how to farm money or materials quickly requires you to actually use the tools the game gives you to study your opponents and work up a strategy.  When you start to see how the systems work together it becomes a giant rabbit hole of discovery.  

The story is refreshingly "low-stakes" for a superhero setting, and the conflicts are firmly grounded at the street level.  No Galactus type threats here, which means the storyline stays character driven.  The writing is solid, the characters have clear motivations and pursue their goals accordingly, and the game spends just enough time on the story to give you context without taking too much time away from gameplay. However, it is important to note that the major plot line does remain unresolved (a sequel is currently in development).  

The graphics and music give the game a unique atmosphere I can only describe as "cel-shaded noir." Think Humphrey Bogart meets Golden Age Batman, but with significant Eastern influence.  The vibe is immaculate, and does much to sell the game on its own merits.  

Areas I felt needed improvement: the amount of time needed to 100% this game is staggering.  This is largely due to the fact that the massive number of passive abilities in this game are generally acquired from defeating enemies, many of whom need to be defeated multiple times to gain access.  
The character motivation system in this game seems like an idea that used to serve a purpose but was ultimately trivialized later.  The only reason to engage with the system was for obsessive completionist purposes, and it had no impact on the difficulty of the game if ignored.  
Some of the storyline fights (the one on one duels in particular) are almost entirely up to RNG.  There was very little I could do to make those fights feel like something other than a coin toss, although in most cases winning or losing did not have any impact on progressing through the storyline.  
Learning mastery sets requires a ridiculous amount of money, which means a ridiculous amount of farming.  Whether you're just experimenting with random combinations, or buying recipes from the vendor, it all leads back to a massive currency sink that cannot be managed without running certain missions over and over again.  
Finally, some missions have some pretty crazy difficulty spikes (lookin at you golden beasts!).  Watching a fully optimized team get absolutely bodied because they took one step too many into a blind hallway half an hour into the mission is one of the more frustrating things I've dealt with.  Overall this is mostly because damage values can have extreme ranges depending on what you're targeting and how they defend.  Doing 22k damage on a lucky shot to a target with 7k hp is fun, but doing 1k damage to the same enemy with the same ability because they got to activate a bunch of passives beforehand makes combat feel random unless you take the extra five minutes to review the enemy's stats before you confirm your hit.  More predictability would go a long way.  

If you enjoy tactical RPGs I think this game is a must-have (especially for the price).  I'm eagerly looking forward to the sequel, and wish the developers all the best!

I love strategic games, turn based games etc. For a long time I searched for a game like Xcom/Darkest Dungeon but with actual characters as playable characters instead of just some units I can discard, I have no emotional connection to. Characters that have their own stories, feeling with their own agendas and beliefs, their own lifes. This game is EXACTLY that. 

Story was really, really good imo. Characters are awesome. Story always kept me on my toes, there are some good plot twists here and there. 

For mechanics this game has it ALL. Mastery system is just amazing. You can make the characters in so many ways BUT with their unique styles, classes and abilities they still play accordingly to their character (well if you REALLY want it you can make them something else probably with all the masteries and items but idk if it would be optimal). This is really difficult to achieve. But they've done it. The gameplay really syncs with the characters. 

The game has a TON of content. There are unique beasts to capture, unique gear to find/craft, unique masteries etc. You don't HAVE to do them btw. I only got 1 unique beast and even that wasn't really needed I just equipped whatever dropped and completed the game on Hard. But they bring a lot of new ways to play if you go for them. 

As negatives there is obvious some jank in the game like some things aren't as fluid as AAA games but that's very normal. 

I also think some things maybe removed from the game if it means faster development and tighter focus. For example I don't really think drones and beasts add too much to the game. Game already has way too mechanics. A little bit simpler (especially at the beginning) would make the game easier for newcomers. On this note crafting system should be much simpler imo. It's not complicated per se but there is too much items and too much steps to create top gear. 

I think you've hit some gold with story, characters and masteries but simplying some systems could be better both for you and for more casual players.

Overall I just want to thank the Dev team for this game and their continued support. I still have DLC to play but I just know it will be just as good. I'm really looking forward to see where the story will go.

Edit : Waiting for updates on the next game!!

Edit 2 : I've seen somewhere where a Dev said there were critism that script was too long? Well for me the story, characters and dialogues were the best part of the game. Plus the artwork. Those artworks are really, really gorgeus whoever draws them is a genius. Just wanted to add my opinion.

I don't know why I passed over giving this a recommendation for so long. Honestly, for the value, time, effort the devs put into this and just the sheer amount of game play, that alone makes this a steal at full price. That said, I'm not going to sugar coat it; Its not a game for everyone. Still, the game and characters are wonderful. The story gets deeper than it has any right to. I am not actually a fan of the sequel being made that is going to do away with our loveable cast of characters as it doesn't feel like their story finishes...but that to me is more so because this cast is so amazing I just want to see their story go on and on. 

So...if you like story and can deal with a little mechanical frustration that you can in true RPG fashion outlevel and perform over time, I highly recommend it. Some of the writing can be corny and its a slow burn at first, but the payoffs end game are worth while...and as you can see from my over 400 hours, there is plenty of content and things to do.

It's a good game. I sunk over 100 hours into it and enjoyed those hours, and so feel like that's an easy thumbs up. But I cannot really offer it unqualified praise, since despite being 100 hours, the ending feels sort of like a sequel hook with a large number of loose plot threads that as of now there is no real indication will be resolved.

Not a perfect game, but definitely the sort of game I want more of to exist. An overall interesting twist/evolution of X-COM like combat with more RPG like characters. Decent enough plot, interesting world, and a variety of characters you (probably) want to see more of.

The other demerit I'd note is that it does that JRPG-like thing (I know it's not a JRPG) where the outcome of a battle is often not tied to what actually happened: i.e. you will 'win' and than the enemy will win or run off and this will happen dozens of times. I get why games do that, but I sort of hate it. It's definitely a story where you are along for the ride, and off the top of my head I'm not sure many of the choices matter much (or if they do there's just a right and wrong answer).

It is at the end of the day excellent value though. There is easily >100 hours of content (my >100 hours is a single playthrough), and at a less-than-full-price cost. It has decent art, graphics, minimal bugs, etc. If you want Anime XCOM RPG, give it a try.

It's a little slow to grab your attention but the more you play, the more you see the amount of depth, content and genuinely interesting mechanics that's been put into this game. There's also a wide variety of QoL features that help you streamline the experience.

The only thing i could bash this game for is somewhat uncanny character models but aside from that this is a very competent Korean take on the XCOM formula.

1、敌人太菜了，哪怕是最高难度，配好天赋的角色也能单刷紫色副本。（希望续作来多点强力敌人）

4、很多主线任务难度设计的不错（比如最后主线大战毁灭轮），但是重复体验时不能让自己的角色撤退很难受，虽然所有角色一起过剧情体验更丰富，但是“事件日志”这种给玩家重复刷的模式锁定全部人上场，还是不能自主撤退是真的破坏体验，比如我为艾丽莎辛苦搭配好天赋，想去单刷最后一关试试水平，结果其他角色也要上场占用我操作时间，如果想避免这样的话就要用雷伊炸死自己的角色，还很难炸死已经成型的角色，只能卸下装备和天赋才好自杀，我感到崩溃！！！麻烦给事件日志设置一下可以撤退或者直接能选择上场角色，急急急！
       不知道你们看B站吗？一些喜欢这个游戏的大佬通关游戏后，还会开发角色搭配并进入紫色任务来展示角色强度，我认为这是极好的，可以增加游戏的趣味性并延长游戏的寿命，然而本应承担通关后内容的联合训练却无人问津，就是由于以上的原因，实在让人痛心，衷心希望制作组能尽快解决“联合训练”和“事件日志”的这几个痛点。（话说这也不难吧？）

If you're a fan of turn based tactical games the likes of XCOM, Phoenix Point, Battle Brothers but felt you wanted something more flashy and JRPG like, do not overlook Troubleshooter.

If you are one of the hardened XCOM players, who installs longwar and likes being punished, I doubt this is for you, but for most players you'll have a fun time exploring the systems, getting stronger and developing the characters you like.

The game is not perfect, the translation can be a bit iffy and somethings unclear and the story is serviceable but nothing ground breaking.

All that said, at £20 it is worth a shot and if it is on discount you should definitely try it.

This game has a great comic book aesthetic with good graphics and a complex layer of game mechanics. The developers  should be commended for having objective based missions and I liked how they eliminated save scumming and added a penalty for dying because the entire gameplay is percentage-based RNG, I feel it was a nice twist on the X-COM formula. However, as you peel away those layered mechanics, you are left with a skeleton, bone-dry gameplay that focuses on finding the safest area of cover to hunker down and defeat enemies one by one like shooting fish in a barrel, that gets quite repetitive and boring.

Additionally... 15 hours of gameplay and I still have only 2 characters unlocked and the missions are long and grindy with little variation in gameplay with little to no attention to any type of coherent level design where the challenge is simply to find cover and shoot waves of random respawning enemies. The UI is atrocious.

I'm not a fan of the 12-year-old flavor text and lack of voice acting with artwork that is mobile-game quality. The food mechanics and friendship mechanics in between missions are boring, time-wasting filler that don't respect your time. This game feels less like X-COM and more like a bloated Disgaea with its complex mechanics and grind, which I don't mind, but the gameplay underneath is where this game falls apart.

There's just not enough gameplay content due to its limited level designs that lack verticality or strategy. The drip-feed of characters and their abilities along with slow base building makes what should have been a 60-hour game into a 200-hour repetitive slogfest. Overall, 6/10.

A brilliant game for X-com addicts who want fun without frustration. The 'X-com lite' games Chimera Squad and Phoenix Point remove the pressure of one-wrong-move permadeath and the enthralling tension of the original X-com with it. Troubleshooters eliminates both permadeath and save scumming, with a single save, replayable missions, and characters who bounce back from incineration or decapitation simply by eating some snacks with their friends. The levels are sufficiently large and packed with enemies that the imperative to equip and deploy your troops well remains, but the worst that can happen is redoing the level rather than tediously replaying a whole X-com campaign, often several times over the first few missions.

The mastery, drone crafting and beast training mechanics are richly intricate and almost entirely reversible for alternative builds within a single campaign. Turn-based combat of unique fighters with a panoply of special attacks and abilities unfolds over beautiful maps of graffiti-bright cityscapes, fantastic wilderness and gritty slums, with detailed environmental effects. The level of difficulty and access to new tactical options both ramp up rather slowly, but to a satisfying mid and endgame thoroughly adjustable in difficulty. There are no irreversible strategic options that would make a replay into a different game, but a single campaign can be extended indefinitely with replayable scenarios and an almost superfluously large range of skills. There are very much superfluous systems such as rent, wages and jurisdictions that have very little effect on the game, but other systems such as drones and beasts that could be managed without are worth having for fun and interest.

The plot is certainly the weakest aspect, crammed with platitudes, nonsensical developments and loose threads; the Black Tiger subplot and Albus' internship blues were egregiously daft. The characters absolutely carry the story, however, with an energetic, lovable, improbably dressed but gorgeously designed band of true companions hacking away at the endless hordes, as well as some memorably styled villains. I cared a great deal for all the heroes of this fun, stylish and potentially challenging turn-based game.

If there's a game that makes full use of the expression "best bang for your buck" it's this one.

You will have a lot of gameplay here, and people who enjoy the SRPG genre or come from the XCOM universe will feel at home. While the story is not the most unique or original, you will mostly be here for the strategy and gameplay.

There’s a certain simplicity in the game’s mechanics, and as you progress you will get used to new ones. The tutorial is kind and simple. You won’t need to learn everything at once or read huge walls of text. The pacing is nicely done and it respects the player’s time. Some characters will be unlocked along the way, and while I agree that some of them may be unlocked too late in the game, considering the number of missions available I would say it’s more than okay. It’s up to you how you approach these missions. There are main missions that allow you to advance in the story and plenty of optional missions to level up and stay competitive or even overpowered if you’re into that.

It’s important to check the items you get during these missions, as well as new weapons, new clothes, and everything in between. There are plenty of boxes for you to open during missions, and it’s wise to open them if you are near one. Getting the best equipment possible is a huge help for later missions, and the same can be said for new materials, leveling up your class, or even changing classes. The game offers plenty of freedom for you to experiment through trial and error. As my missions went on, I got a bit tired of hearing the same phrases from my teammates or listening to the same tunes, so I ended up switching to some lofi, and it ended up being such a chill combo. With all due respect to the audio department, after 60 hours some effects got a bit too repetitive, and that’s okay. When I finally beat the final mission, I felt a sense of relief, and some missions can go on for quite some time. Not only that, but I felt some missions had too many enemies. I would have preferred fewer enemies and more strategy with a slower pacing, because when you enter a mission with 40, 50, or more enemies, it feels like the SRPG aspect fades and now I’m just slowly walking to the next enemy.

Speaking of enemies, depending on the missions there’s a nice variety. Not only human soldiers but also thugs, some melee focused, others making use of firearms for medium or long range such as snipers. There are also non-human enemies in less urban environments, which provide a really good change of scenery, something very welcome if you start to feel burned out from the city setting. In the end, I had great fun. I went for the easier difficulty, and I’m glad such a mode exists since I was able to relax and enjoy the story and strategy aspects much more.

对于一款战旗游戏来说《纷争终结者：被遗弃的孩子们》各方面都是属于优异的。
一、剧情
从剧情上本体结束只是结束了主角所处地域三大黑帮割据的局面。（完成了主角父亲当年没完成的事业，）但本体里还有很多故事没有得到回答。例如当年那场灾难的真相？九龙会的九条鲤鱼最终结果？勺子教在卡特的带领下怎么样了？黑虎集团与主角最后是对手还是？等等一系列都还没结束，制作团队的第二部续作是否能解答呢？说实话很期待。
两个DLC《黑魔女与白狮子》和《深红色的乌鸦》讲述了新加入的成员的故事。《黑魔女与白狮子》的结局依旧是延续本体故事悬而未决的状态。《深红色的乌鸦》故事倒是有了一个具体的结束。
《纷争终结者：被遗弃的孩子们》对于每一个主角团队里角色都有很深的刻画。是很多战旗游戏不具备的。主角团队就不多做介绍了，反派角色也有很多令人着迷例如：成为第二勺的卡特，不愿承担重任的约翰，童子杀手露娜，富有责任感的汉森，报复社会的博士帕斯卡。
很多剧情故事之所以会发生游戏是以一种角色回忆来叙述的。通常回忆会发生主线战斗结束后。
二、音乐和插画
说实话音乐我并不是什么品鉴大师，但是《纷争终结者：被遗弃的孩子们》的音乐让我听起来很舒服很有代入感。再来就是插画，游戏中有500多张插画，个人感觉每一张都能作为桌面壁纸的程度，个人在插画这块是纯喜欢。
三、战旗回合制
基本上开一局时间在一小时左右，甚至两小时（不要问为什么知道）。当然如果你玩到后期很精通的情况下有完整天赋很多图半小时足够。地图很大，有些地图有折磨人的高楼狙击手和枪手一堆，这就有点难受了。整体的难度并不算太高，只要不被集火问题不大（新人推图迷雾地带少走几格，以免被大波反应射击带走）。反击、先发制人、反应射击等这类天赋甚至携带，这是你坐牢的原因。
四、人物养成
无论是等级、技能、天赋、装备、宠物这些都可以看到制作团队用心了。每个角色（本体9人。2个DLC3人，一共12人）优势缺点都很明显，侧重培养就容易成型。这方面在游戏里去体验吧。天赋这个东西研究了挺久的时间，因为天赋这个东西他是随机掉落的，非常多。而且有的有固定组合可以增强。这东西会让你花很多时间去思考。
如果要推荐一款现代故事的战旗游戏除了《纷争终结者：被遗弃的孩子们》我想不到其他的了。

There's so much love and care poured into how this world works and how all the characters have to find their place within it. My comparison list with XCOM2 (not comprehensive by all means)

TLDR: 

[+]More extensive skill customizations
[+]Better gameplay UI
[.]Manhwa visual style
[-]Fixed roster (no permadeath) 
[-]Fixed map layout 

Gameplay: 

    [+]Time-based turn system: each individual unit have different delay time between their turn so more dynamic turn order.
    [+]Pods: a pod can alert another pod within certain distance, unless you can wipe out a pod in a single action (not so easy).
    [+][b]Masteries[/b]: comparable to PCs in XCOM 2, but here you have up to 25-30 pieces, which can be equipped and unequipped at will. Some combinations result in a set with special effect(s), these can be discovered throughout the game. Main selling point of this game. 
    [+]Animals/Drones: comparable to SPARKs (can't take cover) but more varieties. Also, they have their set of masteries so lots of possible customizations.
    [+]Gameplay UI: have you ever wonder what is your unit or enemy unit line of sight? Or if your grenade can reach a particular enemy after your move action? Fear not, combat preview mode in this game will show you these information clearly.
    [.]Equipment: apart from fixed stats, each piece equipment in this game have some randomize additional stats to it (usually negligible). There is a crafting system (quite farmy imo) but you can finish the game without it.
    [-]Difficulty: more forgiving, no permadeath, resource is never a bottleneck.
    [-]Replayability: all maps layout are fixed with very little change for enemy unit placements. Also no window breaking, no breakable cover (there are still explodable objects/units). 

Miscs:

    [+]Learning curve: the combat stats/effects are more complicated but every new concept are introduced quite clearly. In-game wiki and enemy information are also very well-done.  
    [.]Music: both games have good music. 
    [-]Cosmetic: as your roster is fixed, not much can be change apart from some costume DLCs. 
    [-]Voice acting: only in Korean.

[h3]Overview[/h3]
Solid game made with love and dedication. My favorite part of the game is the power system, Masteries. It's extremely deep and allows for a huge amount of customization. I'll spend the rest of my review explaining this because it was overwhelming for me at first.

[h3]Masteries[/h3]
Masteries are little circles that go on a character's mastery board to make them stronger. They cost points to put in, so a character with 10 mastery points can equip two that cost 4, and one that costs 2. Masteries are either common (everyone can equip) or race/class/element specific. This means that characters will have a limited (but still massive) pool of masteries to build from. You can't give Albus (the main character and a wind swordsman) lightning or beast masteries.

Masteries range from being simple (hp+, atk+, etc) to complex (new abilities, conditional effects). They're how you give your character counterattack, make their abilities one-shot most enemies, or become an impossible-to-kill tank.

This means there can be a lot of min-maxing. I personally am lazy so I go for class-specific mastery sets.

[h3]Mastery Sets[/h3]
Mastery sets are a particular combination of 4 masteries. Each set provides additional benefits related to the masteries equipped. This means you can chase after mastery sets instead of thinking about each individual mastery. Since a lot of mastery sets have overlap, you can put a bunch of class-specific masteries on, and fill out the rest of your mastery board to complete the sets.

For example, your character gets the [b]Revenge[/b] set when you equip [b]Counterattack[/b], [b]Final Blow[/b], [b]Clean Hit[/b], and [b]Close Combatant[/b] on a character. 
[list]
    [*][b]Counterattack[/b] lets you melee attack an enemy after being attacked. 
    [*][b]Final Blow[/b] makes you always crit against an enemy with less than 33% health.
    [*][b]Clean Hit[/b] makes your blunt attacks (generally fists) deal more damage.
    [*][b]Close Combatant[/b] makes you deal more and take less damage overall.
[/list]
The [b]Revenge[/b] set makes your counterattack deal more damage. While the other 3 masteries are common masteries, because [b]Clean Hit[/b] is a figher-only mastery, this mastery set can only be activated by fighters.

[h3]End of review[/h3]
I focused on the mastery system because that's what makes Troubleshooter unique to me. The rest of the game is very solid, however, and definitely not lacking in content.

少有的以角色build、人物塑造以及剧情推动做为重点的类XCOM策略战棋。

本作拥有同类型中最丰富的角色build空间，玩法丰富的同时，也有着同类型中较为少见的量大管饱型单一关卡。遗憾的是，受限于演出效果，大型关卡的魅力并没有得到很好的展现。

考虑到这类游戏往往没有任何人物塑造与剧情性可言，本作却反其道以此为核心，搭配独特的韩式叙事，至少也得是个加分项了。

本作也有一些显著的缺点，比如美术层面精细不足，UI也充斥着廉价的网游风格。在平衡性上，个别数值（尤其格挡）简直是用脚填的。

但总体上无论何种难度，在经过仔细的角色bulid与队伍搭建之后，玩家总是可以找到一定程度的平衡感。

何况某些角色在合适条件下，总是能够达到接近无双但又无法真正无双的地步，因此论最高难度与紧迫度，大概是不及那些以难度闻名的同行的。

总而言之，这是一款充满着独特魅力的韩式日系二次元策略战棋大作，而不只是所谓的xcom代餐。

策略战棋爱好者必品。
